title: Pure relative dimension descends to a finite stage
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and limit $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Fix $i_0\in I$ and a morphism $f_0:Y_0\to Z_0$ over $S_{i_0}$, where $Y_0,Z_0$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $f_0$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Write $f_i:Y_i\to Z_i$ and $f:Y\to Z$ for its base changes to $S_i$ ($i\ge i_0$) and $S$, respectively [def-pc-fibre-product]. For an integer $d\ge0$, suppose every nonempty scheme-theoretic fibre of $f$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has pure dimension $d$ [def-weil-pure-dimension]. Then there is $i\ge i_0$ such that for every $j\ge i$, every nonempty fibre of $f_j$ has pure dimension $d$. No flatness, separatedness or properness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0EY2, lemma-descend-dimension-d, in Situation situation-descent-property; persistence for all later stages is Tag 02NK, morphisms.tex, lemma-base-change-relative-dimension-d, with definition Tag 02NJ (definition-relative-dimension-d).

proof.text: Restrict to the cofinal directed tail $I_{\ge i_0}$ and set $Y_i=Y_0\times_{S_{i_0}}S_i$, $Z_i=Z_0\times_{S_{i_0}}S_i$. The scheme-over-limit lemma gives affine transitions and limits $Y,Z$. By qcqs permanence, $Y_0,Z_0\to S_{i_0}$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and so are their base changes; hence $Y_i,Z_i$ are qcqs. Likewise $f_0$ is quasi-compact, and base change preserves this and local finite presentation. A finitely presented algebra is a quotient of a polynomial algebra in finitely many variables, hence finitely generated; thus each $f_i$ is of finite type. The comparison $Y_j\to Y_i\times_{Z_i}Z_j$ is an isomorphism: its inverse is induced by the projection to $Y_i\to Y_0$ and the projection to $Z_j\to S_j$; both composites are identities by fibre-product uniqueness. In particular it is a closed immersion. These verify the structural hypotheses of the finite-stage bound for bases $Z_i$ and sources $Y_i$.

Apply the pure-base-change constructible-image lemma to $f_0$ and its base change $f$. Its dimension-bound conclusion gives $\dim Y_z\le d$ for every limit fibre, including empty ones. The finite-stage fibre-dimension bound now gives $i_1\ge i_0$ with all fibres of $f_{i_1}$ of dimension at most $d$. Restrict to the cofinal upper tail $I_{\ge i_1}$; the limit remains $f$.

Apply the constructible-image lemma to $f_{i_1}$ and its base change $f$. It gives the constructible subset $E=Y_{i_1}\setminus\{y\mid\dim_y((Y_{i_1})_{f_{i_1}(y)})\le d-1\}$ and image containment $\operatorname{im}(Y\to Y_{i_1})\subseteq E$, also for $d=0$.

Apply the constructible-containment lemma to the system $(Y_j)_{j\ge i_1}$, its limit $Y$, the stage $Y_{i_1}$, and $E$. It gives $i\ge i_1$ such that for every $j\ge i$ the image of $Y_j\to Y_{i_1}$ is contained in $E$.

At this index $i$, $f_i$ is the base change of $f_{i_1}$ along $Z_i\to Z_{i_1}$. The fibres of $f_{i_1}$ have dimension at most $d$, and the image of $Y_i\to Y_{i_1}$ lies in $E$. Local fibre dimensions are nonnegative integers here, so the complement defining $E$ is precisely the locus of local fibre dimension at least $d$. The high-dimension-image criterion therefore gives pure $d$-dimensional nonempty fibres for $f_i$. For every $j\ge i$, $f_j$ is the base change of $f_i$ along $Z_j\to Z_i$; pure-relative-dimension base change gives the conclusion.
